commentary_segments.text: A 4th-order Mash (or cascaded) topology has four filter sections for 4th order noise shaping. Only two of them are in a single feedback loop. Stability is easily achieved. It has three outputs however, which are fed to a so-called noise-cancellation circuit. This means that the three outputs must receive the right gain and the right delay so that the noise cancels. Matching will now be an issue. However, many realizations have shown that matching is not really a problem.
